note: Every fact checked on the NASA Ingenuity Mars Helicopter page (challenge resource).

facts.text: After riding to Mars strapped beneath the Perseverance rover (launched 30 July 2020 from Cape Canaveral; landed 18 February 2021 in Jezero Crater), Ingenuity set its four feet on Mars on 3 April 2021.
facts.sourceName: NASA Science: Ingenuity Mars Helicopter (challenge resource)

facts.text: Ingenuity survived its first night on Mars on 4 April 2021, and spun its rotors for the first time on 8 April 2021.
facts.sourceName: NASA Science: Ingenuity Mars Helicopter (challenge resource)

facts.text: A solar panel charged lithium-ion batteries, giving enough energy for one 90-second flight per Martian day.
facts.sourceName: NASA Science: Ingenuity Mars Helicopter (challenge resource)

facts.text: Ingenuity has a mass of 1.8 kg, and its rotors are about 1.2 m tip to tip.
facts.sourceName: NASA Science: Ingenuity Mars Helicopter (challenge resource)

facts.text: Ingenuity flew successfully in the extremely thin Martian atmosphere.
facts.sourceName: NASA Science: Ingenuity Mars Helicopter (challenge resource)

facts.text: On 19 April 2021 Ingenuity made the first powered, controlled flight on another planet, a feat called a Wright Brothers moment.
facts.sourceName: NASA Science: Ingenuity Mars Helicopter (challenge resource)

facts.text: Ingenuity took its first photo of the Perseverance rover on 25 April 2021.
facts.sourceName: NASA Science: Ingenuity Mars Helicopter (challenge resource)

facts.text: Ingenuity was designed as a technology demonstration of no more than five test flights in 30 days. The technology demonstration was complete on 7 May 2021.
facts.sourceName: NASA Science: Ingenuity Mars Helicopter (challenge resource)

facts.text: Ingenuity then became an aerial scout for scientists and rover planners, previewing areas of interest for Perseverance; its first scouting flight was on 24 July 2021.
facts.sourceName: NASA Science: Ingenuity Mars Helicopter (challenge resource)

facts.text: Ingenuity completed 72 flights across nearly three years.
facts.sourceName: NASA Science: Ingenuity Mars Helicopter (challenge resource)

facts.text: In all, Ingenuity flew 128.8 minutes, covered 17.0 km, and reached altitudes as high as 24.0 m.
facts.sourceName: NASA Science: Ingenuity Mars Helicopter (challenge resource)

facts.text: Ingenuity flew for the last time on 18 January 2024. The mission ended on 25 January 2024.
facts.sourceName: NASA Science: Ingenuity Mars Helicopter (challenge resource)
